A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable and describe the same GAT/Aff-Grasp work. However, v2 references supplementary material containing implementation details, generalization tests and additional analyses that is neither appended nor embedded in the supplied PDF. Shared material supports comparison, but those portions remain unavailable.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original AED segmentation results, component ablations and real-world robot experiments, including 179 manipulation trials.

after.justification: Section 4 retains original segmentation and robot results and adds measurements of inference efficiency with and without DFI.

M1.justification: The core architecture, losses and data-collection pipeline remain. Limited revisions to the stated procedure change erosion from the object mask to the tool mask and drop the largest-area condition from object selection in Section 3. These wording changes specify different operations but do not establish an implementation overhaul or experimental rerun.

E1.justification: Both retain Epic-Kitchens/Ego4D, the 721-image AED with 13 object and eight affordance classes, and seen-object, unseen-object and cluttered robot scenarios. However, v2 additionally refers to unseen-affordance generalization tests in unavailable supplementary material, preventing verification of whether distinct evaluation coverage was added.

E2.justification: The AED tables retain DeepLabV3+, PSPNet, SegFormer, ZegCLIP, DINOv2, ViT-Adapter and OOAL. Robot comparisons retain LOCATE and Robo-ABC. Reduced qualitative montages do not establish changes to the methods evaluated in these experiments.

E3.justification: v2 adds parameter-count, GFLOP and latency measurements for DFI inference configurations. However, training and robot protocols are deferred to missing supplementary material. Retention or revision of v1's 15-epoch training, preprocessing and per-object trial procedures cannot be verified, leaving the overall extent of protocol changes uncertain.

E4.justification: The component ablation in v1 Table 6 is retained as v2 Table 4, and v2 Table 5 adds DFI efficiency analysis. v2 refers further ablations and robustness evidence to unavailable supplementary material, preventing comparison with v1's depth-representation, classifier-embedding and hyperparameter studies and detailed robustness cases.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports training seeds, repeated-training uncertainty, confidence intervals or statistical significance tests. Shared results retain single segmentation scores and robot success counts and percentages.

E6.justification: In the corresponding AED tables, ViT-Adapter's mIoU/F1/accuracy changes from 48.36/64.66/65.80 to 50.86/66.88/65.21; OOAL changes from 52.72/68.70/65.79 to 54.82/70.58/68.00. GAT and shared robot results remain unchanged. v2 adds DFI profiling results, including 10.1 versus 6.3 ms inference. The PDFs do not explain the revised baseline scores.

T1.justification: The DFI cross-attention equations, low-rank parameterization and combined focal/dice objective retain their mathematical substance. v2 abbreviates standard loss formulas and the LoRA explanation; it introduces no new assumptions, theoretical derivations or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract reduces the claimed mIoU advantage from 15.9 to 13.8 points, consistent with the revised OOAL result. The automated collection, GAT and Aff-Grasp contributions and the 77.1% overall grasping claim remain; cross-domain and zero-shot generalization receive greater emphasis.

C2.justification: The supplied v2 omits v1 Sections 5.1–5.2, including substantive qualifications about noisy annotations and manual screening, texture and shape confusion, grasping failures, and applicability. It adds explanations for selecting visual-affordance comparators and for their unavailable interaction results. The documented limitations and interpretation are substantially reduced.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies three stem convolutions and selection of the highest-scoring grasp. However, v1's GPU, optimizer, preprocessing, training and robot-hardware details are absent from the supplied v2, which directs readers to supplementary implementation details. Without that material, relocation cannot be distinguished from broader changes in reproducibility information.

R1.justification: v2 substantially narrows the literature discussion by removing the separate survey of supervised, weakly supervised and geometry-based affordance learning. It adds positioning against multi-label egocentric mapping and fine-grained annotation work, acknowledging that some predecessors address one of its two targeted gaps, and adds newer embodied-robotics literature. These exceed bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are rewritten around three challenges. Related work and the conclusion are compressed, numerous numbered subsections become run-in headings, and detailed experimental exposition is replaced by supplementary references. This substantially changes the narrative structure.

P2.justification: The document is extensively recomposed into a compact conference-style layout. Figure 1 gains robot-deployment examples; qualitative montages are reduced and rearranged; tables are resized and relocated; and a new DFI efficiency table appears. These are substantial visual changes beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: v2 offers more focused framing and useful quantitative DFI efficiency evidence. However, the supplied PDF omits v1's detailed limitations and relies on unavailable supplementary material for substantial experimental and reproducibility information. Whether that evidence was preserved or revised cannot be established, so the gains cannot be reliably weighed against reduced transparency and completeness. Revised baseline scores alone do not establish improved quality.
